papers.title: An Infinite Family of Ap\'ery-like Recurrences for Euler's Constant
papers.abstract: Euler's constant $\gamma$, also known as the Euler-Mascheroni constant, remains one of the most elusive constants in mathematics. Despite extensive study, its irrationality is still unproven, and Ap\'ery-like approximations of it are remarkably scarce. We present a novel identity that expresses $\gamma$ in terms of a Meijer G-function and its first few derivatives. This identity is then generalized and used to systematically generate infinitely many Ap\'ery-like approximations of $\gamma$ using a Conservative Matrix Field construction based on the Meijer G-function.

papers.title: Covering plane curves over finite fields with lines
papers.abstract: We prove that, for every fixed $d\geq 2$ and $\varepsilon>0$, the $\mathbb{F}_q$-points of a geometrically irreducible reflexive plane curve of degree $d$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$ can be covered by at most $\left(\frac{1}{d}+\varepsilon\right)q$ many $\mathbb{F}_q$-lines, provided that $q$ is sufficiently large. The same conclusion holds for $\mathbb{F}_q$-irreducible curves that are not geometrically irreducible, since they have only $O(d^2)$ $\mathbb{F}_q$-points. In particular, for sufficiently large $q$, the bound applies to every $\mathbb{F}_q$-irreducible plane curve of degree $d$ when $\operatorname{char}(\mathbb{F}_q)>d$. Our bound is asymptotically sharp. The proof combines Entin's Chebotarev density theorem for varieties over finite fields with the Pippenger--Spencer theorem on covers of nearly regular hypergraphs.

papers.title: Campana strong approximation on generalised Markoff surfaces
papers.abstract: For every smooth projective generalised Markoff surface $X_m$, every hyperplane section $H$, and every integer $n\ge2$, we establish Campana strong approximation with the Brauer--Manin obstruction for $\bigl(X_m,(1-1/n)H\bigr)$.

papers.title: Weighted, GIT and N\'eron--Tate heights on genus-two moduli and Jacobians
papers.abstract: We compare three heights attached to a curve of genus two: the weighted height of its Igusa--Clebsch invariants, the GIT height of a binary sextic defining it, and the N\'eron--Tate height on its Jacobian. For a morphism from an abelian variety to a weighted projective space we define a weighted N\'eron--Tate height and show that the weighted height differs from it by a linear form and a bounded function; the linear form vanishes when inversion is induced by an automorphism of the weighted projective space. For binary sextics we prove the explicit inequality $h_{\inv}\le h_{\text{GIT}} + \frac{1}{2} \log 302$, with nonnegative local differences at the finite places that vanish at places of good reduction. We then construct a family of semistable binary sextics over $E\times E$, where $E:y^2=x^3-2$, whose relative Jacobian carries a section of infinite order, and we show that the Jacobian over the base point is absolutely simple. Along every curve in the parameter space through the base point, the N\'eron--Tate height of the section is a positive multiple of the weighted moduli height up to an error of square-root size, and up to a bounded error when the curve is rational. As applications, we obtain explicit families of genus-two Jacobians of positive rank over $\mathbf{Q}$, an infinite congruence lattice of fibres of positive height, and canonical-limit formulas along elliptic curves in $E\times E$.

papers.title: The Tate Conjecture for Ordinary Calabi-Yau Threefolds
papers.abstract: We use the theory of canonical lifts to prove the integral geometric Tate conjecture for ordinary Calabi-Yau threefolds over finite fields, and also for divisor classes on certain ordinary Calabi-Yau varieties.

papers.title: Co-rank $1$ Arithmetic Siegel--Weil III: Geometric local-to-global
papers.abstract: This is the third in a sequence of four papers, where we prove the arithmetic Siegel--Weil formula in co-rank $1$ for Kudla--Rapoport special cycles on exotic smooth integral models of unitary Shimura varieties of arbitrarily large even arithmetic dimension. Our arithmetic Siegel--Weil formula implies that degrees of Kudla--Rapoport arithmetic special $1$-cycles are encoded in the first derivatives of unitary Eisenstein series Fourier coefficients. In this paper, we make the reduction from global arithmetic intersection numbers for special cycles to the local geometric quantities in our companion papers. Building on our previous companion papers, we also propose a construction for arithmetic special cycle classes associated to possibly singular matrices of arbitrary co-rank.

papers.title: Co-rank $1$ Arithmetic Siegel--Weil IV: Analytic local-to-global
papers.abstract: This is the fourth in a sequence of four papers, where we prove the arithmetic Siegel--Weil formula in co-rank $1$ for Kudla--Rapoport special cycles on exotic smooth integral models of unitary Shimura varieties of arbitrarily large even arithmetic dimension. Our arithmetic Siegel--Weil formula implies that degrees of Kudla--Rapoport arithmetic special $1$-cycles are encoded in the first derivatives of unitary Eisenstein series Fourier coefficients. In this paper, we pin down precise normalizations for some $U(m,m)$ Siegel Eisenstein series, give local Siegel--Weil special value formulas with explicit constants, and record a geometric Siegel--Weil result for degrees of complex $0$-cycles. Using this, we complete the proof of our arithmetic Siegel--Weil results by patching together the local main theorems from our companion papers.

papers.title: Improved, sublinear projective Schwartz-Zippel and (sub)quadratic dimension growth bounds in arbitrary codimension
papers.abstract: We introduce a sublinear sharpened version of a classical projective variant of the Schwartz-Zippel bounds. Here, the sublinearity is in the degree, whereas the classical Schwartz-Zippel bounds are linear in the degree. We prove such sublinear bounds in several cases, including for unions of linear varieties. These bounds lead to a subquadratic dependence on the degree for projective dimension growth bounds in low dimensions. This improves on the quadratic dependence obtained by Binyamini, Cluckers and Kato in [BCK25] and thus brings the dimension growth upper bounds and lower bounds for the worst case closer together, a question asked by Cluckers and Glazer in [CG25]. We also address another question from [CG25], to treat the case of general codimension. To this end, we introduce a natural projection argument with pull-backs. We also give our main results for any global field instead of just $\mathbb{Q}$.

papers.title: Matrix Kloosterman sums and product-trace estimates for semisimple algebras
papers.abstract: Let $k=\mathbb{F}_q$, $E=\mathbb{F}_{q^n}$ and $\mathrm{Tr}=\mathrm{Tr}_{E/k}$. For $r\ge 2$, $a\in k^{\times}$ and $x\in E^{\times}$, let $\mathrm{N}(E,r,x,a)$ be the number of $r$-tuples $(x_1,\cdots,x_r)$ in $(E^{\times})^r$ satisfying $x_1\cdots x_r=x$ and $\mathrm{Tr}(x_1+\cdots+x_r)=a$. We prove $\left|\mathrm{N}(E,r,x,a)-\left((q^n-1)^{r-1}+(-1)^r\right)/q\right|\le (r^n-1) q^{\frac{(r-1)n-1}{2}}$. This proves the square-root estimate predicted in Wan's conjecture and generalizes a previous result of Moisio and Wan. For a finite semisimple algebra $B=\prod\limits_{i=1}^s M_{d_i}(\mathbb{F}_{q^{n_i}})$ over $k$ and a regular element $x\in B^{\times}$, the same method combined with Zelingher's formula leads to analogous square-root estimates.

papers.title: Khintchine dichotomy for images of self-similar measures and almost random walks
papers.abstract: Following the celebrated breakthrough in B\'enard-He-Zhang, we prove Khintchine dichotomy for push-forwards of self-similar measures on $\mathbb{R}^d$ under uniform $C^{1+\alpha}$ maps. For this, we also study almost random walks on $\mathrm{SL}(d+1,\mathbb{R})/\mathrm{SL}(d+1,\mathbb{Z})$ and prove their effective equidistribution.

papers.title: Counting with Hiccup Sequences
papers.abstract: The $(0,x,1,2)$-hiccup sequence starts at $x$ and increases by 1 when the current index has already appeared as a value, and by 2 otherwise. We prove directly that for $x\geq3$ the gaps between its missing values are $1,2,3,\ldots$, each repeated $x-2$ times, and we derive closed formulas, an explicit error bound, and a generating function in terms of Ramanujan's theta functions. The counting functions of the complements satisfy nested recurrences. The sequences of missing values are the partial complements of polygonal numbers. In particular, the $(x-2)$-fold composition of the enumeration of the positive integers that are not $x$-gonal is the hiccup sequence minus 1. We extend the nested recurrence and a tree interpretation to every miss increment $z\geq2$ and every initial value $x\geq2$. Further interpretations involve polyomino vertices, monochromatic pairs, and, by a theorem of Bickle, Ramsey core numbers.

papers.title: Weak and genuine A_n-formality for number fields
papers.abstract: We introduce weak $A_n$-formality for Galois cochain algebras and, for profinite groups whose mod-$p$ cohomology is concentrated in degrees at most two, characterise weak and genuine $A_n$-formality through finite embedding problems and the projective system they form. We then study $A_n$-formality for number fields. Let $K$ be a number field and let $p$ be an odd prime with $\mu_p\not\subset K$. For $p\geq 5$, and for $p=3$ under a natural local cyclotomic condition, we prove that every associated finite $A_3$-embedding problem is solvable. In contrast, for every odd $p$ with $\mu_p\not\subset K$, we show that no compatible family of finite-stage solutions exists, and hence $C^\bullet(G_K,\mathbb F_p)$ is not genuinely $A_3$-formal. The proof uses Chebotarev density, governing fields, and the Gras-Munnier criterion to obstruct the compatibility of finite-stage solutions, and it builds on previous work of Maire-Min\'a\v{c}-Ramakrishna-T\^an. This shows that genuine $A_3$-formality detects a global compatibility obstruction for number fields invisible to every individual finite embedding problem and invisible to obstructions arising from individual strong Massey vanishing problems.

papers.title: Reasonable bounds for Restricted Polynomial Progressions in $\mathbb F^n_p$
papers.abstract: Given an integer $k \geq 2$ and a prime $p$ large enough depending on $k$, we show that, if $A \subseteq \mathbb F^n_p$ does not contain a restricted polynomial progression of the form \begin{align*} x, x+\begin{pmatrix} y_1 \\ y_2 \\ \vdots \\ y_n \end{pmatrix}, x+\begin{pmatrix} y_1^2 \\ y_2^2 \\ \vdots \\ y_n^2 \end{pmatrix}, \ldots, x+\begin{pmatrix} y_1^{k-1} \\ y_2^{k-1} \\ \vdots \\ y_n^{k-1} \end{pmatrix}, \end{align*} where $x \in \mathbb F^n_p$ and $y \in \{0,2, 3, \ldots, M_k\}^n \backslash \{\vec{0} \}$, for some fixed $M_k$, then $A$ must have density bounded above by $\frac{C}{(\log^{(k^{O(k)})} n)^c}$, where $C, c>0$ only depend on $k$ and $p$. For $k\geq 4$, the best previously known bound came from the density Hales--Jewett theorem and was of inverse Ackermann type. The proof uses a recent inverse theorem for noise stability of Bhangale, Khot, Liu and Minzer, which arose in the study of constraint satisfaction problems. The main new ingredient is a proof that the underlying distribution counting restricted polynomial progressions does not admit a nontrivial abelian embedding.

papers.title: Odd order cases of Chowla's averages over arbitrary rectangles
papers.abstract: Let $\lambda$ be the Liouville function. In this paper we prove an average form of Chowla Conjecture for even $k $. that is, for every fixed even integer $k\geq 2$, we prove that \[ \lim_{\min\{M,N\}\to \infty}\frac{1}{MN}\sum_{m=1}^M\sum_{n=1}^N\lambda(m)\lambda(m+a_1n)\cdots\lambda(m+a_kn)=0. \] We construct a stationary model for both averaging variables, derive the finite conditional-entropy estimates. A comparison of overlapping intervals on the logarithmic axis then forces this function to vanish.

papers.title: On the Quantitative Bounds of Nonlinear Roth Theorem
papers.abstract: We prove that any subset $A \subseteq \{1, \dots, N\}$ lacking non-trivial polynomial progressions $(x, x + y, x + y^2)$ satisfies $\lvert A \rvert \le CN \exp\bigl(-c(\log \log N)^\beta\bigr)$ for effective absolute constants $C, c, \beta > 0$. The argument develops a density increment framework localized to anisotropic quadratic Bohr sets. To handle mixed linear and quadratic frequencies, we establish a multilinear transference principle coupled with a relative quadratic inverse theorem based on Balog--Szemer{\'e}di--Gowers additive energy rigidity. Boundary stability across increments is maintained via semi-algebraic model regularization using cylindrical algebraic decomposition and Cauchy--Crofton estimates, while dimension growth is controlled by dissociated basis reduction and multidimensional Erd{\H{o}}s--Tur{\'a}n--Koksma equidistribution.

papers.title: Regularization of a Divergent Arithmetic Product via the Asymptotic Monoid: The Case of $(-1)^{\omega(n)}$
papers.abstract: We apply the generalized monoid of words and logarithmic-prefix functionals of \cite{C1} to the regularization of the divergent product \[ P_{\omega}=\prod_{n=1}^{\infty} n^{(-1)^{\omega(n)}}, \] where \(\omega(n)\) is the number of distinct prime divisors of \(n\). The associated Dirichlet series \(D_{\omega}(s)=\sum_{n\ge1}(-1)^{\omega(n)}n^{-s}\) has a natural boundary at \(\Re(s)=0\), as established by Meretov (1987) and recovered here as a special case of the Estermann--Dahlquist theory of Euler products, which makes zeta regularization impossible: the derivative \(D_{\omega}'(0)\) does not exist. This product therefore lies completely beyond the reach of classical regularization methods. We construct the canonical net encoding the sign sequence, define the logarithmic-prefix functional with exponent \(\alpha=2\), and extract a finite value through the weighted evaluation functional of the monoid framework. The evaluation functional is shown to converge absolutely, and this convergence is unconditional: it follows from the classical zero-free region of \(\zeta(s)\) (de la Vall\'ee Poussin), which yields the effective bound \(T_{\omega}(x)=O(x\,e^{-c\sqrt{\log x}})\) for some \(c>0\). Numerical computation up to \(N=10^7\) gives the regularized value \[ P_{\omega,\mathrm{ren}}\approx 0.7731, \] a new constant of arithmetic origin that cannot be obtained by any classical summation method. We also compute the second derivative of the Dirichlet series at \(s=1\), \[ D_{\omega}''(1)=8\,C_2\ln 2, \] where \(C_2\) is the Hardy--Littlewood twin prime constant, which provides an unconditional analytical link to the arithmetic structure of the sequence \((-1)^{\omega(n)}\). A self-contained proof of the natural boundary, based on the Estermann--Dahlquist theorem, is given in Appendix~A.

papers.title: The Davenport constant of balls and boxes
papers.abstract: Given an additively written abelian group $G$ and a set $X\subseteq G$, we let $\mathsf{D}(X)$ denote the Davenport constant of $X$, namely the largest non-negative integer $n$ for which there exists a sequence $x_1, \dots, x_n$ of elements of $X$ such that $\sum_{i=1}^n x_i =0$ and $\sum_{i \in I} x_i \ne 0$ for each non-empty proper subset $I$ of $\{1, \ldots, n\}$. In this paper, we mainly investigate the case when $G$ is $\mathbb{Z}^2$ and $\mathbb{Z}^3$, and $X$ is a discrete Euclidean ball. An application to the classical problem of estimating the Davenport constant of a box - a product of intervals of integers - is then obtained.

papers.title: Approximating $1$ by Sums of Unit Fractions
papers.abstract: If a finite collection (with repetitions allowed) of unit fractions has sum larger than $K$, how close can a sum of some of them come to $1$ from below? Improving a bound of Erd\H{o}s and Graham, we prove that the gap is at most $\exp(-c\sqrt{K\log K})$ for an absolute constant $c>0$ and all sufficiently large $K$. The proof combines equal fractions and applies a Fourier estimate to groups of denominators with comparable contributions. Elementary divisor counts then give the bound.

papers.title: Remarks on the Geometry of Sets in $\mathbb{Z}^d$ with Small Fourier $L^1$ Norm
papers.abstract: We study geometric inverse problems for finite sets $A\subset \mathbb{Z}^d$ whose Fourier $L^1$ norm, or Wiener norm, \begin{align*} \|A\|:=\int_{\mathbb{T}^d}\Big|\sum_{a\in A}e(a\cdot t)\Big|dt \end{align*} is subpolynomial in $|A|$. In particular, we show a variety of geometric phenomena are incompatible with small Fourier $L^1$ norm. Our principal application concerns spherical Freiman models. Suppose $\|A\|=|A|^{o(1)}$ and $D\subseteq A$ is Freiman isomorphic to a set $S$ of lattice points on a sphere; then, $|D|/|A|$ must be polynomially small in $|A|$. Moreover, if $|D|/|A|$ is not too small, almost all of $S$ lies in a small number of spherical caps, and almost all caps have rich additive structure. The proof uses a new mechanism for studying additive structure across subsets of $A$, along with decoupling results of Bourgain-Demeter.

papers.title: On the Moments of Least $s$-Gaps of Partitions and a Conjecture of Baruah and Talukdar
papers.abstract: Andrews and Newman \cite{AN19, AN20} defined the minimal excludant or mex of a partition. The mex of a partition is the smallest positive integer which is absent from the partition. Baruah, Bhoria, Eyyunni and Maji \cite{BBEM} studied the sum of mex split according to parity, together with its $\ell$-th moments. Ballantine and Merca \cite{BM20} generalized mex to the least $s$-gap, which is the smallest natural number that does not occur minimum $s$ times in the partition. Baruah and Talukdar \cite{BT} conjectured a corresponding asymptotic equivalence between the sums of odd and even least $s$-gaps for every $s>1$, generalizing a theorem of Barman and Singh \cite{BS} for the classical mex. In this article, we derive exact formulas for the $\ell$-th moments of $\smex(\pi)$ for every fixed $\ell\ge 1$, in terms of partition functions. We give a complete proof of the conjecture of Baruah and Talukdar \cite{BT} for every natural number $s>1$. We also generalize an identity of Hopkins, Sellers and Stanton \cite{HSS} to the least $s$-gap setting.

papers.title: On $m$-fullness in number fields
papers.abstract: We prove asymptotic formulas for the number of $m$-full ideals of bounded norm in a given ideal class and for the number of $m$-full algebraic integers of bounded Weil height.

papers.title: Properness of the Cuspidal Hilbert Eigenvariety
papers.abstract: We prove that for any prime $p$ and tame level $N$, the weight map from the cuspidal Hilbert eigenvariety constructed by Andreatta-Iovita-Pilloni for a totally real field $F$ to the weight space is proper in the sense of Buzzard-Calegari, under a non-vanishing hypothesis on certain Sen polynomials of Galois representations at the primes above $p$. In particular, this yields the properness of the eigenvariety away from non-positive integral Sen weights. Our approach extends the $p$-adic Hodge-theoretic argument of Diao-Liu.

papers.title: A cyclotomic gluing construction for lattice sphere packings
papers.abstract: For a positive integer $d$, let $\Delta_d^L$ denote the supremum of the densities of lattice sphere packings in $\mathbb R^d$. We prove that, for every sufficiently large $d$, $\Delta_d^L \gg d^2\log\log d\,2^{-d}$. Abuya-Gargava-Zhao obtained the same bound along a sparse sequence of dimensions by combining Venkatesh's cyclotomic symmetries with Klartag's stochastic ellipsoid method. We introduce a multi-cyclotomic gluing construction that allows this argument to work in every sufficiently large dimension.

papers.title: Hankel Matrix Decompositions and Digital Sequences over Function Fields
papers.abstract: This paper studies formal Laurent series, with particular emphasis on their continued-fraction and Laurent-series expansions. Knowledge of both expansions is important, for example, in the study of Kronecker-type sequences in uniform distribution theory and in the search for potential counterexamples to variants of Littlewood's conjecture over fields of formal Laurent series. Our approach investigates Hankel matrices over a field and relates them to Laurent-series expansions over the same field. We describe such matrices via a block $\mathcal{L}\mathcal{B}\mathcal{U}$ decomposition, using recursive algorithms based on the continued-fraction coefficients of the corresponding Laurent series. The upper-triangular factor $\mathcal{U}$ has several remarkable properties. In particular, it is constructed columnwise from the so-called Ostrowski-type representations of powers of $X$. Applying $\mathcal{U}$ in Niederreiter's digital construction yields an Ostrowski-type van der Corput sequence that can be related to the corresponding Kronecker-type sequence. For ordinary Kronecker sequences, such a relation is known in only one case, that of the $(n\varphi)$-sequence. The original motivation for our study of Hankel matrices was to recast the search for counterexamples to variants of Littlewood's conjecture over fields of Laurent series as the search for specific Kronecker-type sequences. Interestingly, the method developed for the study of Kronecker-type sequences also allows a new perspective on the celebrated Sobol' construction. Our approach yields a short and elegant proof of its excellent distribution properties.

papers.title: Polynomial parametrization of $\text{SL}_2$ over global function field rings
papers.abstract: We combine the universal polynomial matrix identities of Larsen--Nguyen with Trost's arithmetic lemmas to obtain polynomial parametrizations of $\text{SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S})$ for every global function field $K$ and every nonempty finite set of places $S$. The additional ingredient is a function-field cancellation lemma, proved using ray class fields and Chebotarev in odd characteristic and the perfectness of finite residue fields in characteristic two. The proof also gives a polynomial matrix over $\mathbb{Z}$ that works simultaneously for all these rings.

papers.title: A Rigid Analytic Curve Can Have a Dense $p$-adic Orbit
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal D$ be a product of Drinfeld upper half spaces and let $J$ be the corresponding product of projective linear groups acting on $\mathcal D$. We prove that if $Y$ is a reduced, quasi-compact separated strict $\mathbb C_p$-analytic space and $f: Y\to\mathcal D$ is analytic with $\dim Y<\dim\mathcal D$, then $J f(Y(\mathbb C_p))$ is closed and nowhere dense in $\mathcal D(\mathbb C_p)$. The quasi-compactness assumption is necessary even when the source is a strict rigid analytic curve, while a quasi-compact perfectoid source can still have an orbit closure with nonempty interior. For every finite extension $F/\mathbb Q_p$ and $d\geq3$, we construct a closed smooth irreducible non-quasi-compact curve in $\Omega_F^{d-1}$ with dense orbit under a fixed diagonal one-parameter subgroup. We also construct a $\mathbb Q_p$-defined analytic map from the open unit disc to $\mathbf P^2$ with dense $\operatorname{PGL}_3(\mathbb Q_p)$-orbit, and an analytic map from a one-dimensional affinoid perfectoid torus to $\mathbf P^2$ whose $\operatorname{PGL}_3(\mathbb Q_p)$-orbit closure has nonempty interior.

papers.title: A conditional bound $\Lambda\le0.13963$ for the de Bruijn--Newman constant
papers.abstract: Assuming that $\zeta(s)$ has no nontrivial zero with $\mathrm{Re}\, s > 7/8$, as asserted in a recent unrefereed preprint of OpenAI, we obtain $\Lambda \le 13963/100000 = 0.13963$ for the de Bruijn-Newman constant. A published Polymath boundary computation supplies a finite-region strip of half-width $1/5$. We derive an approximation on $3 \le \mathrm{Im}\, z \le 6$ from its general Riemann-Siegel coefficient bounds. At height $61/20$, a fixed cutoff permits two differentiations, and comparison with $\zeta$ bounds both the zero-density kernel and its vertical derivative. A new conjugate-pair inequality and a twenty-four-step strip comparison give the stated bound. The finite scalar and polynomial certificates are included in the paper; earlier comparisons giving $0.17973$, $0.17172$, and $0.16408$ are retained to show the source of the gain. The argument uses neither Gordon's analytic inputs nor Gomila's new computations. The seven-eighths hypothesis remains an assumption, and the published numerical boundary input is retained.

papers.title: Reciprocal LCM powers and Robin's criterion
papers.abstract: For $\kappa > 1$, we study the reciprocal LCM-power function \[ \sigma^{[\kappa]}_{-1}(n) := \sum_{d \mid n}\mu(d)\,\sigma_{-1}(n / d)^\kappa. \] We determine its average and extremal orders. A natural Robin-scale normalization is strictly increasing in $\kappa$ and tends to $\sigma_{-1}$, yielding an RH-equivalent criterion. Unconditionally, the corresponding Robin inequality holds eventually on every bounded parameter interval. Directed interval arithmetic proves the inequality for each $n > 5040$ and $1 < \kappa \le 100{,}000$.

papers.title: On the Imaginary Part of $\zeta'/\zeta$
papers.abstract: We derive an explicit zero-side formula for the imaginary part of a smooth truncation of the logarithmic derivative of the Riemann zeta-function. The resulting kernel is the odd companion of the Fej\'er kernel in Montgomery's pair-correlation identity. Motivated by the recent breakthrough of Anthropic's Claude \cite{Claude26}, we also give an expository account of how the real-part identity can be turned into a matrix problem, overcoming the clustering obstruction for zeros off the critical line. Finally, we discuss how the new imaginary-part identity may contain additional information about such clustering.

papers.title: Product and Quotient Set Dominance in Finite Groups
papers.abstract: A classic problem in additive number theory asks whether a given subset of integers has more sums or differences. This inquiry naturally extends to finite groups, where one compares the sizes of the product set $AA$ and the quotient set $AA^{-1}$ for a subset $A \subseteq G$. A finite group is considered product-dominant if it contains a higher proportion of subsets where $|AA| > |AA^{-1}|$, and quotient-dominant if the reverse is true. We establish statistical criteria to determine the dominance behavior of large finite groups by analyzing the moments of the random variable $d(A) := |AA| - |AA^{-1}|$. By translating product and quotient relationships into graph-theoretic constructions, we compute these moments through counting independent sets. Our main result demonstrates that for a growing sequence of finite groups $G_k$ with center size $Z_k$ and involution count $T_k$, the condition $Z_k = o(T_k)$ implies the groups are eventually product-dominant. Conversely, if $T_k \cdot \sqrt{3}^{R_k/Z_k} = o(Z_k)$ (where $R_k$ denotes the number of elements whose square is central), the groups are eventually quotient-dominant. Using these asymptotic conditions, we resolve the Miller--Vissuet conjecture by proving that all dihedral groups $D_n$ for $n \geq 3$ are product-dominant. Furthermore, we classify the dominance behavior of several major families of groups, proving that symmetric groups and non-abelian finite simple groups are product-dominant, while groups of odd order and certain abelian groups are quotient-dominant. Finally, for groups that fall outside our asymptotic conditions, we derive an explicit formula for the first moment utilizing the irreducible characters and conjugacy classes of the group.
